name: Runtime_SetInterruptHandler
domain: Installs or removes one interrupt-dispatch-table entry and its REG_IE (and, for VBlank/HBlank/V-Counter, REG_DISPSTAT) enable bit.
expressed: rejects index > 13 with no side effects (no IME touch, immediate return)
saves REG_IME, disables it, and restores it at every exit from the valid-index path
clears bit `index` of REG_IE, then sets it back only if handler is non-NULL

for index 0-2 (VBlank/HBlank/V-Counter) also clears the matching REG_DISPSTAT IRQ-enable bit (bits 3/4/5); for index==2 specifically it additionally clears/replaces the V-Count trigger byte (bits 8-15) from the vcount argument, and re-sets the enable bit only if handler is non-NULL
writes handler (if non-NULL) or the reserved no-op dispatch stub (if NULL) into Data_030000e0[index], the 14-entry interrupt-dispatch table
evidence: games/gs1/asm/0800307c.s's literal pool holds 0x04000208/0x04000200/0x04000004 (REG_IME/REG_IE/REG_DISPSTAT, already named this way in games/gs1/recon/en/main/serial_runtime_family.h and games/gs1/recon/en/main/0800300c.c), 0x030000e0 (the 14-entry interrupt-dispatch table Func_0800300c DMAs into IWRAM from ROM 0x08007320, per games/gs1/recon/en/main/0800300c.json), and 0x08003009 (Func_08003008 / RuntimeDispatch_ReservedNoOp03008, games/gs1/src/runtime/dispatch/reserved_no_op_f.c, plus the thumb bit -- the same reserved no-op the DMA'd table already installs as its default entry).

This owner is already forward-declared 'void Func_0800307c(s32 index, s32 priority, InterruptHandler handler)' in serial_runtime_family.h and called from three already-recovered owners, which is what pins every parameter's role: games/gs1/recon/en/main/08005d10.c has 'Func_0800307c(7, 0, Func_08006240)' (index 7, second argument unused so 0, a real handler pointer); games/gs1/src/link/serial/remove_serial_irq_handlers.c has 'Func_0800307c(7, 0, (InterruptHandler)(handler = 0))' and 'Func_0800307c(handler, 0, 0)' with handler==6 (NULL handler to remove a slot, second argument still unused so 0); games/gs1/src/unidentified/main/system/system_owner_5.c has 'Func_0800307c(2, 0, 0)' (index 2 = V-Counter, disable); and games/gs1/src/unidentified/main/field/field_owner_104.c has 'Func_0800307c(2, 136, (InterruptHandler)address)' -- index 2 is the V-Counter IRQ and 136 is a plausible V-Count scanline value, which is what identifies the second parameter's V-Count role and confirms it is only meaningful for index==2.

Hand-traced instruction-by-instruction against games/gs1/asm/0800307c.s: the >13 bound, the REG_IE bic/orr-by-mask pattern, the 8<<index / vcount<<8 REG_DISPSTAT pattern (with the mask-narrowed-to-0xff-only-when-index==2 byte-clear), and the table-write-with-fallback-to-the-reserved-stub pattern all match the retained assembly's control flow and constants exactly; only instruction scheduling/register allocation and one specific literal-load shape (below) differ from the reference bytes.

The family-matcher's best (low-confidence, 7318/10000, below this project's 7500 transplant threshold) guess games/gs1/src/graphics/palette/advance_cycle.c was read in full: no shared callees, field offsets, or constants with this owner -- a shape-only false positive (the AdvancePaletteCycle body is an unrelated palette-cycling routine over a completely different global-state struct), consistent with this session's prior finding that even above-threshold family matches are frequently false positives. Not used as evidence.
credible_shapes_tried: Baseline field-by-field C89 rewrite using s32 locals for saved_ime/mask/ie/bit/clear_mask/dispstat (u16 locals were tried first and rejected: they made the compiler emit an extra sign-extending lsls/asrs #16 pair around every intermediate value, which s32 locals -- truncated only at the final volatile-u16 store -- avoid): 140 candidate bytes, 66 differing halfwords, 48 wrong instructions.

Reordering the REG_IE section to read REG_IE (`ie = REG_IE;`) before computing the shift (`mask = 1; mask <<= index;`) instead of computing the mask first: realigned that whole section (movs r2,#1 / ldr r4 / ldrh r3 / lsls r2,r0 / bics r3,r2) to match the reference byte-for-byte in instruction shape. Adopted.

Merging the DISPSTAT block's separate `bit` and `set_bits` locals (which start equal and only diverge for index==2) into one reused local: removed a redundant `adds r4,r3,#0` register-to-register copy the two-local version produced, and made `movs r4,#8 / lsls r4,r0 / mvns r2,r4` match the reference exactly. Adopted; dropped wrong_instructions from 48 to 40, candidate size 140 -> 136.

Data_030000e0[index] write, else-branch variants: a shared `InterruptHandler *slot = &Data_030000e0[index];` used by both branches, and a `InterruptHandler def = ...; Data_030000e0[index] = def;` temp-then-store form -- both changed the else-branch's internal ldr/lsls ordering but net regressed (candidate grew and the branch polarity/shared-join structure diverged further from the reference's separate-branches-to-one-join shape). Rejected; kept the plain direct `if (handler != 0) Data_030000e0[index] = handler; else Data_030000e0[index] = default;` form, which already matches the then-branch exactly and is off by only one instruction's position in the else-branch.
remaining: Every remaining byte of the 64 differing halfwords / 40 wrong instructions traces to one root cause: 'REG_IME = 0;' (the interrupt-disable at function entry) compiles on this owner's route to `ldr r2,[address]; ldrh r3,[r2]; adds r6,r3,#0; ldr r3,[pool 0]; strh r3,[r2]` (loading the constant 0 through a pooled halfword), while the reference instead reuses the already-loaded address register itself as the store source -- `ldr r3,[address]; ldrh r2,[r3]; adds r6,r2,#0; strh r3,[r3]` -- storing 0x04000208 truncated to 16 bits (0x0208) into REG_IME, which still functionally disables IME since the hardware only implements bit 0 (clear here). Confirmed this is not a mistake in this draft specifically: the minimal isolated statement `*(volatile u16*)0x04000208 = 0;` alone, compiled through this project's default routing (equivalently explicit `--family gcc296`) for an unregistered source, ALSO produces the pooled-halfword-load shape, not the reference's self-store -- and games/gs1/recon/en/main/0800300c.c's own already-committed draft (a sibling owner, same statement, same 'canonical-gcc296' route per its own dossier) shows the identical pooled-halfword-load shape for its own 'REG_IME = 0;', diverging from ITS OWN reference's plain `movs r5,#0; strh r5,[r6]` in the same way -- so this is a pre-existing, shared, unexplained residual class across at least two owners in this translation unit, not something specific to this draft's source shape. Tried and rejected as fixes: `REG_IME = (u16)(u32)&REG_IME;` (self-referential cast, hypothesizing the compiler might CSE the address computation into the store) -- produced byte-identical output to plain `=0`, i.e. GCC re-derives a fresh pooled constant for the second use rather than reusing the register live from the first read; explicit `--family old-agbcc` (matches games/gs1/src/save/atmel/erase_sector.c's own real, exact-adopted `saved=*(vu16*)ADDR; *(vu16*)ADDR=0;` idiom, confirmed by direct candidate-show comparison to legitimately compile to plain `mov r0,#0; strh r0,[r1]`) -- correct plain-movs shape, but NOT the reference's self-store, and old-agbcc is very unlikely to be this owner's real route given its immediate, gapless adjacency to 0800300c (0x0800300c + 112 = 0x0800307c exactly), which is already established canonical-gcc296; `--flags -O1` / `--remove-flags -O2 --flags -O1` on the isolated statement -- produced byte-identical output to -O2, no effect. This residual, and its cascade (the extra pooled halfword forces GCC to insert an early inline literal pool plus a branch-over and alignment padding after the REG_IE store, which then phase-shifts every subsequent pc-relative literal offset and, per objdiff's raw-instruction alignment, every downstream instruction in the printed diff -- none of which are independent additional errors), account for the entire measured gap. No length mismatch beyond this single 12-byte overage (136 vs 124); every field value, branch condition, and call/store target matches the reference algorithm exactly.
notes: No inline assembly, fixed-register variable, compiler barrier, forbidden ABI, copied instruction bytes, or compiler modification was used.
